_status: MOCK / GOLDEN FIXTURE -- see _notes before using in CI
_notes: ReasoningAgent.generate_insights() (agents/reasoning/agent.py) calls an actual LLM (settings.generator_model, default 'gpt-4o') via app.services.llm_provider with structured output enforced by `instructor`. An LLM call is not deterministic byte-for-byte even at temperature 0 across providers/versions, so this cannot be derived the way stages 1-4 were derived from the project's own deterministic code.

What IS deterministic and regression-testable: (a) the evidence_pool passed to the model, built by build_evidence_pool()/build_observation_evidence() from 05_expected_normalized_entities.json -- every 'obs-TEMP-XX' id and its text below is exactly what that function produces from this fixture set's coded entities (trend evidence is empty per 06_expected_trend_output.json, so only obs-* and guideline-* entries appear); and (b) the post-processing agent.py performs on whatever the LLM returns -- it drops any candidate citing an evidence_id outside the pool, and re-derives supporting_entity_ids from the cited evidence's entity_ids rather than trusting the model's own UUIDs (see agent.py module docstring).

'mock_llm_response' below is what a stubbed llm_provider.llm(...) call should return in a test (matching LLMInsightResponse's shape in agents/reasoning/models.py); 'expected_draft_insight_set' is the DraftInsightSet this codebase's own _to_draft_insights() would deterministically produce FROM that stubbed response plus the evidence pool -- so once llm_provider is mocked with 'mock_llm_response', this section becomes a legitimate exact-match regression assertion, not a guess.

supporting_entity_ids values are the real, currently-computable uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, f'lmis:entity:{document_id}:{temp_id}') values for document_id=11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 (see agents/reasoning/evidence.py::_entity_id_for and agents/trend/agent.py, which use the same scheme).
